title: UA Agro - Live Operations
description: Sections 15 and 19's operations view. Ordered by what an operator looks at first during a peak-season rush: are calls being served, are they fast enough, is anything on fire.

panels.title: Calls in flight vs capacity
panels.description: Section 3 expects a 5-10x seasonal peak. The capacity line is drawn so headroom is visible rather than inferred.

panels.title: Turn latency p50 / p95 vs the section 7 ceiling
panels.description: The 1200 ms threshold is section 7's ceiling, drawn on the panel so a breach is visible without reading the axis.

panels.title: Latency by segment (p95)
panels.description: Section 7's budget, segment by segment. This is the panel that turns 'the agent is slow' into 'Deepgram is slow', which is the difference between a guess and a fix.

panels.title: ASR confidence by language
panels.description: Section 19: surfaces which districts have accent or noise problems. A language whose confidence sits low is one whose quality tier is optimistic.

panels.title: Transfers by reason
panels.description: Section 12's triggers. The shape of this chart is how an operator tunes thresholds against real data rather than intuition: a spike in low_recognition_confidence is a line-quality problem, not an agent problem.

panels.title: Containment vs transfer
panels.description: The pair an operator judges the agent by. Shown together because either alone misleads: perfect containment with an unhappy caller base is not success.

panels.title: Safety triggers (section 16.1)
panels.description: Not an error metric. Each one is a farmer who reported a poisoning and a P0 ticket needing human review within the hour.

panels.title: Cost per call
panels.description: Section 8's worked example is 6.65 rupees for a 3-minute Hindi call. Upward drift is usually the answer cache having stopped working.

panels.title: Validator rejections
panels.description: Section 16.3's last line. A rise means the layers above it, the tools and the prompt, have stopped doing their job.

panels.title: Unhandled intents
panels.description: Section 11.2's improvement loop. A rising count is not a fault: it is the agent meeting questions nobody anticipated, and the queue an operator works through.
